newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cost-cutting steps lift Viag 1996 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Cost-cutting steps lift Viag 1996 earnings.

text.p: German diversified utility Viag AG reported higher 1996 sales and earnings on Friday and said its 1997 result would rise again despite start-up losses in its telecommunications business.

Viag said in a statement 1996 operating profit before tax rose to just under 2.4 billion marks from 2.1 billion marks, according to provisional figures, while sales rose to about 42.5 billion marks from 41.9 billion marks.
The figures were largely in line with analyst forecasts.
The group has undergone a programme of restructuring aimed at trimming costs and improving Viag's market position, and these measures would continue to lift earnings and turnover at the group.
"As a result we are optimistic of continuing to increase sales in the current year and to hold earnings at a high level, despite unavoidable start-up losses in telecommunications," Viag said.
Viag plans to keep its 1996 dividend unchanged at 12 marks.
Peter Antes, utilities analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich, said: "These figures are within our expectations and we are keeping Viag at "market neutral".
Vereinsbank is maintaining its forecast earnings per share (EPS), based on the German DVFA analysts' method, at 36 marks per share for 1996 and 39 marks per share in 1997.
Vereinsbank's Antes said he was keeping its 1997 EPS outlook relatively high because he believed the company was being cautious in its outlook.

Lynn Reinhardt, utilities analyst at BZW in Frankfurt, said that not too many conclusions could be drawn from these preliminary figures, but she said the figures, and the company outlook, were within her range of forecasts.
"Internal growth has not been that great, they have just been adding new companies, so we will have to see what the full figures in May have to say," said Reinhardt.
Viag is involved in a range of activities, including power generation, the manufacture of packaging and chemicals, distribution and logistics and telecommunications.
The year 1997 will see the implementation of projects to improve the group's portfolio and expand in the telecoms area.

The telecommunications issue has been a contentious one for Viag in recent days. Viag has a telecommunications alliance with British Telecom and the alliance was recently awarded Germany's fourth digital cellular telephone licence.
However, unconfirmed press reports that BT has been in secret talks with rival German utility Veba AG have hit Viag shares of late, which were down two marks at 707 marks in early bourse trade.

Among Viag subsidiaries, its Bayernwerk utility unit posted a five percent rise in 1996 sales to 9.58 billion marks, while Viag said operating profit grew at a higher rate, with the profitability increase mainly down to cost-cutting measures.

Its majority-owned specialty chemicals unit SKW Trostberg, which listed its shares on the bourse in 1995, posted sales of 3.873 billion marks in 1996, compared with 3.875 billion marks the previous year.
Viag said that sales lost through disinvestments in SKW's natural foodstuffs business were compensated by higher construction chemicals sales. No 1996 operating profit figure was given.
Schmalbach-Lubeca AG, which manufactures beverage containers, provisionally reported an operating profit of 118 million marks in 1996, with no sales figures given.
A cooler summer dampened sales of beverage containers, but this was offset by cost-cutting measures which helped boost Schmalbach's operating profit.
